lessons: The narrow completion seam is the enforcement point; messages, receipts, and claims are inert there.

lessons: Enforcement must live at the narrow completion seam (VERIFIED), not at the message layer, so no completion can be recorded without the durable event.
Suppression detection must re-verify the persisted event, not the recorded event_id, so deleting or editing the event file after completion is an integrity failure.
The canonical event store is the authority; the Activity Feed is the projection. A testable event fulfills the feed contract without inventing a competing store.
naya.summary: The execution controller now refuses completion (VERIFIED) unless a canonical Activity Feed event exists, binds to the exact claim and action, carries the durable receipt and successor handoff, and is projected to the Activity Feed; validate() detects suppression and tamper as activity event integrity failures.
